images.title: Property management, *duty by duty*
rows: Answers every prospect with the same facts about the unit and books showings.
Takes the request, sorts it under the triage rules and dispatches the vendor.
Sends reminders, confirms payments and answers questions from the lease.
Sends approved renewal terms on schedule. Legal notices are drafted for a person.
Drafts the monthly summary from the software. The manager sends anything with a decision.
Collects the file and the facts. A person decides.

images.name: weekend
images.title: A Saturday for the *AI property management assistant*
images.roleSub: Reports to the senior property manager
rows: A prospect asks about a two-bedroom listed last night. It sends the facts and books a showing for Sunday at 1 pm.
A tenant reports a dripping kitchen faucet. It logs the work order and schedules the plumber for Tuesday.
Sends renewal offers to four tenants whose leases end in 90 days, with the terms the manager approved.
A tenant asks to split this month's rent into two payments. It writes up the request for the manager.
Two neighbours each message about the same parking spot. It logs both accounts and flags the dispute.
An owner asks whether the HVAC repair at their unit is done. It answers from the closed work order.
"No hot water in 4B." It replies in a minute, opens a work order and books the on-call plumber for Sunday morning, then alerts the manager.

images.name: setup
images.title: How the assistant *is set up*
steps: Decide what it may and may not ask, say and do before any tenant data is connected.
Pull every inquiry, request and question and sort it by type.
What counts as an emergency, who is on call, and what waits until business hours.
Listings, work orders, the rent ledger and the calendar. No applicant reports.
Applications, money, legal notices, disputes and emergencies go to a named person.
It drafts replies and work orders while the manager reads each one, then takes on more.
Update it when vendors, rents, policies or owners change.
